entries.why: A CAP-40 signed-payload signer (P...) has a 68-byte strkey payload. At 79ea2ac the signer column encoder silently keeps 32 bytes, so the row reads back undecodable (#716). At 2a0a84e it rejects the value instead, so the ledger indexes but cannot be persisted (#729). 2c87335 stores it.

Protocol 30 golden whose ledger headers use STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS (StellarValueType 3). go-stellar-sdk v0.7.3, used by 2a0a84e, predates that value; v0.8.0, used by 3e22515, decodes it. The harness must report this as a protocol gap, not as a failure.

Signed-payload signer with a 1-byte payload (40-byte strkey payload). At 79ea2ac it is truncated to 32 bytes on write without error and reads back as a P address that does not decode, the #716 failure. 2a0a84e rejects it (#729); 2c87335 stores it.

Signed-payload signer with a 64-byte payload (100-byte strkey payload). At 79ea2ac it is truncated to 32 bytes on write without error and reads back as a P address that does not decode, the #716 failure. 2a0a84e rejects it (#729); 2c87335 stores it.

One account holds a G signer and a P signer over the same key. Fails with the other P entries before 2c87335 and passes from it on. docs/PLAN.md ties this case to a follow-up of the #729 fix; no failure distinct from #729 reproduces in this harness, so it is pinned as regression coverage.

Payment to a muxed (M) destination. Tried against #716 and it does not reproduce: the payment path stores the base account, so no M address reaches an AddressBytea, even at 79ea2ac (no lossy or normalized value is seen). #716's reachable muxed producer is a muxed source on Soroban operations, which this rule does not build. Pinned as regression coverage.

golden_replay.why: Every protocol 30 golden must index and persist on HEAD with no decode error, indexer error, panic or dropped transaction.
